title: Cell Cycle Checkpoint Control
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Biology
description: Interactive MicroSim showing how cyclin-CDK complexes and checkpoint proteins regulate cell cycle progression, with damage response and p53 mutation scenarios

learningObjectives: Explain how cyclin-CDK complexes regulate cell cycle progression
Predict what happens when checkpoint proteins fail
Compare G1/S and G2/M checkpoint requirements
Analyze the consequences of p53 mutations on cell cycle control
prerequisites: Cell cycle phases (G1, S, G2, M)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration with hover tooltips and toggle scenarios
keyQuestions: What happens to cell division when DNA damage is detected?
Why does Cyclin B drop sharply at anaphase?
How does p53 mutation contribute to cancer?
commonMisconceptions: Cyclins are always present at the same level throughout the cell cycle
A single checkpoint failure is sufficient to cause cancer
G1/S and G2/M checkpoints check for the same conditions
assessmentOpportunities: Identify which cyclin-CDK pair controls each transition
